meta_models.name: Muse Glimmer 30B
meta_models.note: Tuned and tested by ta-amps; the live workers run Muse Spark 1.3 through the Meta API.
meta_models.role: Fills in Task Object forms and tool calls exactly, so a worker's report fits the queue the first time.

tested.text: Exact tool-call match rose from 93.3% to 99.3% on our 150-case test, tuned and measured on Kaggle on two T4 GPUs.

uses.text: One fine-tuned Muse Glimmer 30B for search, review, routing and tool calling. On held-out tests it picked the right Task Object 89% of the time (base 2%), reviewed submitted work at 99% balanced accuracy (base 28%; it wrongly accepted 2 of 126 flawed reports), split nonprofit requests into Tasks at 98% F1 (base 45%), and kept tool calling at 99% (base 94%)
Reviewer under the rule of two: sent back every self-review case and 124 of 126 flawed submissions (99% balanced accuracy on 204 held-out reviews; the 2 misses were reports with too few claims)
Search and retrieval: picking the right Task Object for a plain-language need went from 1.7% to 89.1% (top choice, 175 held-out needs)
Routing: splitting a nonprofit's request into Tasks, Task-Object F1 45.0% to 97.8% (106 held-out requests)
Tool calling inside the same adapter: 94.0% to 99.3% exact match on the fixed 150-task evaluation

Ready for a 5% trial on checking finished work. On 107 held-out reviews it scored 98.5% balanced accuracy, against 92.0% for Muse Spark 1.3 on the same reviews. With two simple rule checks run first (at least three claims, and the not-legal-advice line on legal topics), it sent back every flawed report and passed every good one in that set.

rules: Meta first: every step defaults to a Muse model through the Meta API, at the standard tier (owner, Nov 1).
Name models, not agent apps. An agent app (Muse Code, nanoMuse, OpenClaw...) is not a model. Agent apps appear only in the 'Volunteers' AIs' table on this page.
A * marks a model that is not Meta's: a fallback, or a model used only in tests.
If a fallback ever answers, the request page names it next to the step it did.
No receipts, hashes or run ids on the page. Dates, durations, counts and versions only.
